question: Why is 30 degrees Celsius not considered twice as warm as 15 degrees Celsius?

options.A: Because Celsius measurements have uneven gaps between numbers
options.B: Because the scale lacks a true absolute zero point
options.C: Because thermal energy cannot be measured numerically
options.D: Because temperature is actually measured on a nominal scale

question: What is the main difference between the ureters and the urethra?

options.A: Ureters store urine, while the urethra filters waste products from the bloodstream
options.B: Ureters and urethra perform the exact same task on opposite sides of the pelvis
options.C: Ureters carry urine from kidneys to the bladder, while the urethra carries urine outside the body
options.D: Ureters pump urine out of the body, while the urethra connects the kidneys directly to the outside

explanation: Think of ureters as the pipes coming down from the kidneys to the bladder, and the urethra as the final exit tube to the outside world! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h1)

question: Which muscle group makes up the main bulk of the pelvic floor?

options.A: Levator ani
options.B: Piriformis

options.D: Gluteus maximus

question: Why does practicing assertiveness help reduce workplace burnout in nursing?

options.A: It forces hospital management to increase your salary
options.B: It guarantees that you will never work night shifts
options.C: It stops doctors from ever questioning your care plan
options.D: It prevents unvoiced frustrations from building up

explanation: Voicing concerns early stops resentment and chronic stress from overwhelming your mental health. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h3)

question: What standard p-value do nursing researchers usually look for to prove statistical significance?

question: Which of these is a great example of an informal community leader?

options.A: An elected federal minister of health in the capital city
options.B: A traditional village chief or respected religious cleric
options.C: A government-appointed local government area chairman
options.D: A licensed environmental health sanitation officer

explanation: Informal leaders don't carry government appointment letters; they lead because of deep respect, culture, tradition, or religion in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why does the intestinal wall have a muscular layer (the muscularis)?

options.A: Secreting hormones into the bloodstream
options.B: Generating peristaltic waves to move contents
options.C: Filtering waste from local blood vessels
options.D: Absorbing digested sugars and amino acids

explanation: These muscles squeeze in a coordinated wave pattern (peristalsis) to push food smoothly along the digestive tract. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is taking good care of ward equipment so important for your patients?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to pay for broken items
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for hospital biomedical engineers
options.C: It ensures devices provide reliable therapy and diagnostics
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about machinery

explanation: When equipment is well-maintained, it works accurately and keeps our patients safe from harm or wrong results. Great job keeping your patients safe! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the medical term for the procedure where the vaginal opening is narrowed by sealing the cut labia?

options.A: Infibulation
options.B: Excision
options.C: Cauterization
options.D: Clitoridectomy

question: A nurse is feeling very anxious after a traumatic patient incident on the ward. Where should they turn for immediate, supportive help from fellow health workers?

options.A: The public relations department for media statements
options.B: The legal department for liability review
options.C: A hospital-sponsored peer support team
options.D: The billing office for patient records

explanation: Peer support teams are specially trained to offer a comforting shoulder and an empathetic ear when ward incidents shake your confidence. [learn more](GST319_U6_T4#GST319_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT an advantage of using a checklist in nursing research?

options.A: Producing structured data that is easy to score
options.B: Being quick and straightforward to administer
options.C: Providing deep, emotional life stories of patients
options.D: Reducing subjective wandering during clinical observation

explanation: Checklists capture neat, measurable data—they aren't designed to tell deep, open-ended emotional stories. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h7)

question: What is a key duty of a nurse acting as a facilitator in a community?

options.A: Punishing community members who refuse to take their medications
options.B: Demanding immediate resignation of corrupt hospital directors
options.C: Writing new national health laws without community input
options.D: Connecting marginalized groups with health resources and social programs

explanation: Spot on! As a facilitator, your job is to bridge the gap—connecting people who need help with the exact services and agencies that can provide it. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h3)

question: Which type of parasitic egg is known for having a little lid (operculum) or a sharp spine?

options.A: Trematode ova
options.B: Nematode ova
options.C: Bacterial spores
options.D: Cestode ova

explanation: Flukes, or trematodes, lay eggs with a tiny lid or spine to help the larva escape. Spot on! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h3)

question: What is the main job of the support nurse when family members are allowed in the room during an active emergency resuscitation?

options.A: To write down every single drug given by the doctor
options.B: To chase all visitors out of the hospital building
options.C: To do chest compressions if the main rescuer gets tired
options.D: To explain procedures, offer comfort, and answer the family's questions

explanation: Spot on! Having a dedicated nurse look after the family keeps them informed and calm, leaving the rest of the team free to focus fully on saving the patient. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why do doctors prescribe medications for heart failure if they don't completely cure the disease?

options.A: To reduce heart workload and slow disease progression
options.B: To replace the need for dietary sodium restriction
options.C: To permanently repair damaged heart valve tissue
options.D: To cure the underlying viral infection in the muscle

explanation: Great thinking! Since heart muscle doesn't easily repair itself, these drugs are lifesavers because they make the heart's job much easier and help patients live longer, more comfortable lives. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is your immediate priority action if the umbilical cord slips out (prolapses) during labor?

options.A: Manually lift the baby's head off the cord to restore blood flow
options.B: Push the visible cord gently back inside the uterine cavity
options.C: Clamp and cut the umbilical cord immediately on the spot
options.D: Instruct the mother to push as hard as she can with contractions

explanation: Keeping pressure off the cord with your hand keeps oxygen flowing to the baby while you prep for urgent delivery. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is a half-way house primarily designed to be?

options.A: A high-security prison for individuals with criminal records
options.B: A transitional residential facility for recovering individuals
options.C: An acute emergency ward for violent psychiatric patients
options.D: A permanent housing estate for elderly retired nurses

explanation: Great job! A half-way house acts as a gentle stepping stone between intensive hospital care and fully independent living in the community. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h2)

question: A nurse is preparing a patient for an emergency cesarean section in a busy unit. What is the best way to use the safety checklist?

options.A: Pause and verify each safety step out loud with the surgical team
options.B: Ignore the checklist because the team is in a hurry to save time
options.C: Ask the patient to fill out the surgical checklist by herself
options.D: Sign the checklist at the end of the shift without checking the patient

explanation: Checklists are most effective when the healthcare team pauses to verify items collaboratively out loud before proceeding. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why are vital sign trends over several hours more useful than a single reading?

options.A: They prevent the need to perform laboratory blood tests
options.B: They take less time for the nurse to chart
options.C: They show whether the patient is improving or getting worse over time
options.D: They guarantee that the electronic monitor is working correctly

explanation: Brilliant nursing insight! Tracking patterns helps you catch subtle warning signs before a patient takes a turn for the worse. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which test is mostly used to confirm if a patient has fluid or consolidation in their lungs?

options.A: Chest X-ray
options.B: Abdominal ultrasound
options.C: Electrocardiogram
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging

explanation: A simple chest X-ray is fast, easy, and gives a clear picture of cloudy areas or fluid buildup in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why are confidentiality and safe spaces so vital when caring for survivors of violence in a hospital?

options.A: To encourage survivors to share their experiences without fear of stigma or retaliation
options.B: To hide the crime from law enforcement agencies
options.C: To ensure the hospital avoids paying taxes on patient care
options.D: To speed up the discharge process for the patient

explanation: You got it! Survivors are often terrified of exposure or payback. A safe, confidential space helps them build trust and speak out. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is an effective community nursing strategy to help stop FGM?

options.A: Inspecting every household's private rooms every single week
options.B: Punishing mothers publicly for crimes committed by elders
options.C: Banning all community meetings and traditional gatherings in villages
options.D: Promoting alternative rites of passage that celebrate maturity without cutting

explanation: Spot on! Offering safe, positive ways to celebrate cultural milestones helps communities keep their traditions alive while dropping the dangerous cutting. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h7)

question: Why should outbreak control measures sometimes start before lab results are fully finalized?

options.A: To avoid paperwork and administrative meetings
options.B: Because laboratory tests are always completely inaccurate
options.C: Because doctors are not allowed to read lab reports
options.D: To prevent further spread and save lives immediately

explanation: Waiting for lab work during a fast-moving crisis can cost lives. Taking action early based on clinical signs is a lifesaver! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h6)

question: Which level of prevention uses routine immunizations to stop a disease before it even starts?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention is all about stopping health problems before they begin—vaccines are a classic example. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h5)

question: What is a major economic driver pushing children onto the streets in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive funding for public primary education
options.B: Strict government enforcement of child rights laws
options.C: Abundant social welfare support for large families
options.D: Widespread household poverty and unemployment

explanation: Spot on! When families struggle to feed themselves due to hard times, kids often have to go out and look for money. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T3#GNS225_U5_T3_h2)

question: Where do bedside nurses usually get the best ideas for a research topic?

options.A: Personal financial investment reports
options.B: Ancient historical nursing textbooks
options.C: Fictional medical television dramas
options.D: Daily clinical observations and ward routines

explanation: Your time on the ward is a goldmine! Noticing what gives patients trouble during your daily shift is the number one way to find real research topics. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of a Patient Classification System?

options.A: To calculate annual facility building taxes
options.B: To categorize patients based on their nursing care needs
options.C: To track hospital utility and electricity usage
options.D: To determine which doctors are on emergency call

explanation: It sorts patients by how sick they are (acuity) so hospitals can figure out how much nursing time is truly required. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h6)

question: An instructor wants to use adult learning principles when teaching IV cannulation. What's the best way to do it?

options.A: Show how the skill solves immediate clinical problems students will face on the ward
options.B: Require students to memorize the history of intravenous therapy before practice
options.C: Ignore student past experiences because healthcare changes too fast
options.D: Use strict punishments and pop quizzes to force compliance with the protocol

explanation: Adults learn best when they see the immediate, practical value of a skill for real-life patient care. Connecting it to ward duties makes it click! [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h6)

question: A patient with paraplegia sits in a wheelchair for hours without shifting weight. What skin problem is most likely to develop over their tailbone area?

options.A: Pressure ulcers
options.B: Pulmonary edema
options.C: Renal calculi
options.D: Muscle hypertrophy

explanation: Spot on. Sitting too long in one position cuts off blood supply to bony parts, leading quickly to painful pressure sores if we don't help them shift. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h8)

question: Which clinical findings form the classic triad of an opioid overdose?

options.A: CNS depression, pinpoint pupils, and respiratory depression
options.B: Dry skin, confusion, and elevated heart rate
options.C: Hypertension, hyperthermia, and dilated pupils
options.D: Diarrhea, excessive sweating, and muscle twitching

explanation: Opioids depress the central nervous system and respiratory centers while typically causing miosis (pinpoint pupils). [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h5)

question: When should a nurse question a doctor's order to start systemic corticosteroid therapy?

options.A: When the patient has an active, untreated fungal infection
options.B: When the patient has stable, controlled blood pressure
options.C: When the patient had childhood asthma
options.D: When the patient has mild seasonal allergies

explanation: Spot on! Because steroids suppress the immune system, giving them during an active infection lets the infection run wild. Always check for infections first! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h6)

question: Is the pH of normal semen acidic, neutral, or alkaline?

options.A: Slightly acidic
options.B: Extremely acidic
options.C: Alkaline
options.D: Neutral

question: Which type of study collects data at just one single point in time?

options.A: Longitudinal study

options.D: Prospective cohort study

question: Which test is primarily used to collect cellular samples for cervical cancer screening?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound

question: What is the coolest superpower of adaptive immunity compared to innate immunity?

options.A: It relies entirely on physical skin barriers to keep germs out
options.B: It creates immunological memory for faster responses to repeat infections
options.C: It provides instant protection within minutes of touching a pathogen
options.D: It does not require white blood cells to eliminate foreign microbes

explanation: Adaptive immunity never forgets a face! It remembers specific germs it has fought before, so if the same germ shows up again, it attacks much faster and stronger. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h2)

question: What is the correct order of assessment techniques for most body parts?

options.C: Inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation
options.D: Auscultation, percussion, inspection, palpation

question: What kind of pressure is normally found inside the healthy pleural space around the lungs?

options.A: Atmospheric pressure
options.B: Fluctuating pressure
options.C: Positive pressure
options.D: Negative pressure

explanation: Great job! The pleural space naturally acts like a vacuum (negative pressure) to keep our lungs nicely expanded against the chest wall. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T18#GNS221_U2_T18_h1)

question: What happens when clinic staff guess tally counts on extremely busy days?

options.B: It causes client folders to physically deteriorate faster.
options.C: It automatically increases the clinic budget allocation.
options.D: It results in the immediate suspension of the senior nurse.

explanation: Guessed data leads to bad government decisions. If the numbers say you treated 50 kids for malaria when it was actually 500, the next drug supply shipment will be way too small! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h5)

question: If a patient lacks intrinsic factor due to stomach damage, what health problem are they at risk for?

options.A: Lactose intolerance
options.B: Type 2 diabetes
options.C: Peptic ulcer disease
options.D: Pernicious anemia

question: Why is it dangerous to press down on a waste bag with your hands to create more space?

options.D: It releases unpleasant odors into the ward

question: Why is the immediate postpartum period considered the most critical time for postnatal care checks?

question: What is the main difference between a medical emergency and a surgical emergency?

options.A: Surgical emergencies never involve internal bleeding

options.C: Medical emergencies only happen outside the hospital
options.D: Surgical emergencies usually require an operation to fix

question: What is the main goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To provide free meals for the entire local community
options.B: To protect and promote the well-being of students and staff
options.C: To replace the need for community primary healthcare centers

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the popular BRAIDED counseling mnemonic?

options.C: Bedrest
options.D: Benefits

question: Why must community members be involved in a community diagnosis?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the local government entirely
options.B: To ensure health programs fit their local culture and needs
options.C: To provide financial funding for hospital construction
options.D: To train as professional medical doctors in the village

explanation: Involving the community helps nurses understand local beliefs and realities, making health interventions much more acceptable and successful. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes inter-sectoral collaboration in immunization?

options.A: Partnering with schools, religious bodies, and local leaders to boost coverage
options.B: Leaving all public health work entirely to the central government
options.C: Working exclusively with doctors inside major hospital wards
options.D: Buying vaccines from international suppliers without local input

explanation: Inter-sectoral collaboration brings different community groups together to work toward shared public health goals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h7)

question: Why did nurse leaders in the 1970s feel the need to build their own unique nursing theories?

options.C: To better explain and guide the unique aspects of professional nursing care

question: What is the primary client for a community health nurse?

options.C: Individual clients who visit the clinic daily
options.D: Only patients admitted to the surgical ward

explanation: Community health nursing focuses broadly on the health and wellness of entire populations rather than just single hospitalized individuals. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h1)

question: What sign tells you a patient is struggling and working extra hard to breathe?

options.A: Warm and dry skin on the forehead

options.C: Symmetrical and slow chest wall rise
options.D: Quiet and relaxed abdominal movement

question: What is the main reason nurses and planners must set priorities?

options.A: Healthcare resources are always limited
options.B: All health problems cost the exact same amount to treat
options.C: Government policies forbid buying new medical equipment
options.D: Doctors refuse to participate in budgeting meetings

question: Why do we need intersectoral collaboration (working with other sectors) to achieve good public health?

options.A: Hospitals are solely responsible for fixing bad roads and cleaning rivers
options.B: The Ministry of Health cannot legally operate without approval from finance officers

question: When public health experts calculate the Maternal Mortality Ratio, what is the standard denominator used?

options.D: Per 1,000 pregnant women

question: Why do doctors and nurses prefer ultrasound when a patient needs repeated scans over a short time?

options.B: It is totally painless and needs no practice
options.C: It gives a much clearer view of bones than a CT scan
options.D: It completely replaces the need for blood tests

question: What is the name of the popular skull traction device that uses spring-loaded pins?

question: A postpartum mother is bleeding heavily, and oxytocin isn't quite cutting it. Which medication must you AVOID if she has a history of chronic high blood pressure?

options.A: Carboprost
options.B: Misoprostol
options.C: Normal saline

question: A patient living in severe poverty with no stable shelter comes in with heavy anxiety. What is likely driving this?

options.A: An acute reaction to a rare genetic blood disorder
options.B: An excess intake of heavy metals found in tap water
options.C: Chronic toxic stress from daily survival struggles
options.D: A sudden allergy to standard hospital room bedding

question: What is a common misconception about the health status of HIV orphans?

options.A: People assume all orphans are infected with HIV themselves

options.C: People think orphans are immune to childhood malnutrition

question: What does 'reliability' mean when talking about a data collection tool in a hospital?

options.A: The tool gives consistent results when used repeatedly by different staff.

question: What is the main focus of community-centred nursing care?

options.B: Conducting laboratory tests for rare diseases

options.D: Treating severe illnesses inside hospital wards

question: Before giving an antibiotic, a nurse scans the patient's wristband and the drug barcode with a handheld scanner. What is this safety step called?

options.C: Barcode medication administration
options.D: Root cause analysis

question: Why do nurses check sensation across different skin areas when assessing a patient with a back injury?

options.C: To map out dermatomes and identify the exact spinal level of injury

question: Why do health organizations strongly oppose 'medicalization'—which is performing FGM in a clinic by trained health workers?

question: Why is it so important for patients to finish their entire course of preventative medication?

question: What is the main purpose of doing a wet mount test on vaginal discharge?

question: What should a nurse do first when planning health education for a patient from a different cultural background?

options.A: Insist that the patient follow hospital routines strictly at home
options.B: Hand out standard English brochures without discussing them
options.C: Assume the patient already knows basic community health rules

question: What is the main catch or limitation of chemical buffer systems?

options.D: They require active nervous system input to initiate action

question: Why do health teams check 'signal functions' instead of just looking at hospital buildings?

question: What is transactional sex?

question: Why are elderly patients much more prone to skin tears?

question: How should a nursing team view a test that doesn't show the expected improvement during the Study phase?

options.A: As a valuable learning opportunity to understand what does not work

options.C: As proof that quality improvement projects are completely useless

question: Which color of waste bag is standard for infectious clinical waste and pathological specimens?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: Blue

question: What usually happens when healthcare workers communicate poorly after a mistake?

options.A: Patients recover much faster from their physical injuries
options.B: Families feel ignored and are more likely to seek legal action
options.C: The hospital administration praises the staff for protecting privacy
options.D: Insurance companies automatically pay out large claims

explanation: When we act defensively or fail to communicate well, families feel disrespected. Out of frustration, they are much more likely to take legal action. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h2)

question: Which brain structure kicks off the hormonal changes of puberty?

options.A: Anterior pituitary

explanation: Spot on! The hypothalamus is the master control center that starts the whole process by releasing puberty hormones. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T2#GNS312_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which touch receptors deep in the skin are best at detecting heavy pressure and fast vibrations?

question: Why do scientific journals use the same standard layout for all research papers?

question: What is often one of the very first warning signs of internal cancers like stomach or pancreatic cancer?

options.D: Sudden visual impairment

question: How does estrogen impact a growing teenager's height during puberty?

question: What is the best way to document your physical findings for an endocrine patient?

options.A: Document only the lab values and skip physical descriptions

question: In a court of law, how is a patient's medical record treated?

question: As a nurse, what is your most critical intervention to catch energy imbalances early in hospitalized patients?

question: What term describes shaky, clumsy, and uncoordinated muscle movements caused by a problem in the cerebellum?

options.A: Akinetopsia

options.C: Aphasia
options.D: Ataxia

question: What is a main reason why children affected by HIV often drop out of school?

options.C: Mandatory admission into vocational training centers

question: What is the main job of a Governing Board in a public health corporation?

question: What is the primary purpose of a pre-leave nursing risk assessment?

options.A: To ensure the patient no longer requires follow-up care

question: Which vaccines does a newborn baby routinely receive right at birth here in Nigeria?

question: Why is it important to remove loose rugs from the home of a patient with dementia?

question: What does profound deafness mean for a patient?

question: In community health nursing, what does the term AEFI stand for?

question: Why must nurses avoid using stigmatizing language when talking about substance use?

question: Which of these best describes a traditional classroom setting in nursing school?

question: What two main elements make up the foundation of modern professional nursing?

question: A woman at 36 weeks pregnant with twins asks for a home birth. What should you, as her midwife, do?

question: Which level of measurement has a true zero point that means none of the item is present?

question: What is the main reason we use a t-test in nursing research?

question: In a regular 28-day cycle, when do we usually check serum progesterone to see if ovulation happened?

question: What is the best way to support parents who are grieving a baby's birth defect?

question: Which sign tells a nurse that a local skin infection is starting to spread through the whole body?

question: Why do doctors prescribe oral contraceptive pills to women with symptomatic uterine fibroids if they don't actually make the fibroids disappear?

question: How do vaccines primarily protect the human body from infectious diseases?

question: Why would you want to conduct a key informant interview with a respected local elder?

question: Which part of the brain acts as the emotional alarm system that triggers the fight-or-flight response during anxiety?

question: What is the name of the popular screening tool used specifically to check nutritional risk in older adults?

question: Which type of drug crosses biological cell membranes the easiest?

question: Why do patients bargain when facing a terminal illness?

question: What do we call large cells with multiple nuclei formed when virus-infected cells fuse together?

question: Why do we need different sectors—like health, law enforcement, and social services—to work together when managing violence cases?

question: Why is surgical repair of a varicocele performed in some infertile men?

question: Why do qualitative researchers include direct quotes from participants in their results?

question: During a traditional diaphragm fitting, what two points does the nurse measure between?

question: Who is the focus of medical isolation compared to quarantine?

question: Why should NGOs involve community members right from the project planning stage?

question: Why do hospitals still rely on high-temperature incineration for certain waste, despite environmental concerns?

question: As a community nurse in a malaria-prone area, which prevention tip should you push the hardest?

question: What is the single best way to stop infectious diarrhoea from spreading in a community?

question: Why is observing chest symmetry important during the breathing assessment?

question: Why should you separate normal general waste from hazardous medical waste right from the start?

question: Before giving another dose of magnesium sulfate, which clinical sign must you check first?

question: What is usually one of the very first warning signs a woman might notice with cervical cancer?

question: Why is it important to connect daily nursing tasks to the broader organizational goals?

question: What is the greatest superpower of using a mixed methods design in nursing?

question: What dangerous habit must nurses watch out for when patients use axillary crutches?

question: How do daily nursing assessments help hospitals track their overall quality of care?

options.A: They replace the need for governmental public health surveillance
options.B: They determine the exact monthly salary of hospital administrators
options.C: They calculate the hospital's annual marketing budget
options.D: They provide the baseline data needed to track pressure injuries and falls

explanation: Hospital quality scores depend heavily on honest, regular nursing notes about things like skin integrity and patient mobility. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the main reason a patient would have a hysterosalpingography (HSG) procedure done?

options.A: To measure circulating levels of follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: To check if the fallopian tubes are open and examine the inside of the uterus
options.C: To visualize ovarian cysts and measure their exact physical dimensions
options.D: To scrape the endometrial lining for suspected malignant cells

explanation: During an HSG, a special dye is gently put into the uterus while taking X-rays. It helps doctors see if the fallopian tubes are blocked or clear. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h6)

question: A patient from a fishing community presents with blood in their urine and lower belly pain. Which parasite is the likely cause?

options.A: Necator americanus
options.B: Enterobius vermicularis
options.C: Schistosoma species
options.D: Ascaris lumbricoides

explanation: Schistosoma parasites can damage the bladder and urinary tract lining, causing blood in the urine (hematuria) and discomfort. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which waste products are eliminated from the body through sweat?

options.A: Excess carbon dioxide and oxygen
options.B: Red blood cells and blood platelets
options.C: Undigested food particles and fiber
options.D: Salt, water, and small amounts of urea

explanation: Sweat contains mostly water and salt, along with minor metabolic waste products like urea. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h6)

question: What do we mean by the term 'opportunity cost' in health economics?

options.A: The profit a pharmaceutical company makes on a new vaccine
options.B: The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made
options.C: The total amount of money a hospital spends on patient medications
options.D: The discount given to patients who pay for medical care in cash

explanation: Think of opportunity cost as what you sacrifice. When you choose to spend your last Naira on transport instead of snacks, the snack is your opportunity cost! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why is achieving small, quick wins important when dealing with a resistant community?

options.A: It allows the nurse to take an extended holiday leave
options.B: It proves that traditional leaders have no real authority
options.C: It forces the local government to increase health sector taxes
options.D: It helps restore faith and revive interest in the health system

explanation: Tangible, early successes demonstrate competence and genuine commitment, helping to break down skepticism and resistance. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h6)

question: How does reading past literature help a nurse choose a new research topic?

options.A: It provides a list of patients who agreed to join the study
options.B: It automatically writes the methodology chapter for the new study
options.C: It proves that all healthcare questions have already been answered
options.D: It helps identify what is still unknown so duplication is avoided

explanation: Checking what others have done saves you from repeating old work and helps you find fresh territory to explore. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h3)

question: A patient is diagnosed with a slow-growing, usually benign tumor that develops from the protective membranes covering the brain. What is it called?

options.A: Pituitary adenoma
options.B: Glioblastoma
options.C: Astrocytoma
options.D: Meningioma

explanation: You got it! Meningiomas grow from the meninges—the protective layers surrounding your brain and spinal cord. They are usually slow-growing and benign, which is great news for the patient. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h2)

question: What is the single best way to stop resistant germs from spreading between patients?

options.A: Keeping patient room windows completely sealed shut
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins to all visitors
options.C: Sprinkling chemical disinfectants on hospital floors hourly
options.D: Performing thorough hand hygiene before and after care

explanation: Never underestimate simple handwashing! It remains our number one defense against carrying germs from patient to patient. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T18#GNS313_U1_T18_h7)

question: If a patient has a very weak immune system, which type of drug do they urgently need to fight an infection?

options.A: Bactericidal
options.B: Bacteriostatic
options.C: Antihistamine
options.D: Topical antiseptic

explanation: Since their immune system can't finish the job, they need bactericidal drugs to directly kill the bacteria for them. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why is clinical relevance so important when reviewing a research paper?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any statistical calculations in the paper
options.B: It proves whether the authors paid their publishing fees on time
options.C: A study can be methodologically sound yet completely useless for your specific patient group
options.D: It guarantees that the journal has a high academic impact factor

explanation: Even if a study is well-designed, we must check if its findings actually make sense and work safely for the specific patients we care for every day. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h5)

question: Your rural clinic keeps losing vaccines because of erratic power supply. What is the best immediate response that uses local community resources?

options.A: Wait for the federal government to rebuild the entire national electrical grid
options.B: Partner with local market leaders to mobilize a solar backup or reliable cold box system
options.C: Close the clinic permanently and refer all children to hospitals in the capital city
options.D: Blame the local residents for failing to generate their own electricity

explanation: Brilliant problem-solving! Instead of waiting for distant solutions, tapping into local networks and leaders helps you find practical, community-driven fixes right away. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is formed at the very end of the clotting process to firmly seal a damaged blood vessel?

options.A: Soluble fibrinogen
options.B: Unbound platelets
options.C: Inactive thrombin
options.D: Stable fibrin mesh

explanation: At the finish line of the clotting cascade, fibrinogen turns into a strong, stable fibrin mesh that holds the blood clot firmly in place like a net. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T15#GNS215_U6_T15_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a post-event debriefing session?

options.A: To celebrate the financial earnings of the event promoters
options.B: To write promotional advertisements for the next gathering
options.C: To punish staff members who made mistakes during the event
options.D: To review operational successes and identify areas needing improvement

explanation: Debriefs are all about learning. The team looks at what went well and what can be improved for the next big event. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T3#GNS315_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why is birth spacing emphasized during family planning counseling for postpartum women?

options.A: It allows the mother's body and nutrient stores to recover fully
options.B: It prevents the mother from ever experiencing menopause
options.C: It guarantees that all future children will be born male
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medical checkups

explanation: Spacing pregnancies gives the mother adequate time to restore her health and nutritional reserves, leading to better outcomes for subsequent children. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h6)

question: Which hormone triggers the tiny muscle cells around the milk glands to squeeze during the let-down reflex?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin is the hormone of love and contraction! It squeezes the myoepithelial cells around the alveoli so milk can flow down the ducts. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T17#GNS121_U5_T17_h6)

question: How do broken elevators and inaccessible buildings directly affect a disabled person's mental health?

options.A: They automatically cure chronic depression by forcing daily exercise
options.B: They improve social bonds by encouraging neighbors to carry people
options.C: They have no impact on emotions, only on physical fitness
options.D: They lead to physical exclusion, which triggers deep loneliness and isolation

explanation: That's right. When buildings aren't accessible, individuals get trapped at home, cutting off their social life and leading to heavy isolation. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T14#GNS225_U5_T14_h5)

question: What is the most important rule for writing the methodology section?

options.A: It must prove that the hypothesis was completely correct
options.B: It must contain enough detail for another researcher to repeat the study
options.C: It must focus heavily on the personal feelings of the participants
options.D: It must avoid mentioning any ethical approval processes

explanation: Good science can be repeated! If your steps are clear, another nurse researcher should be able to run the exact same study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h5)

question: What does consumer purchasing power refer to?

options.A: The physical strength of shoppers carrying heavy bags from the market
options.B: The financial ability of a household to buy goods and services with their income
options.C: The political influence grocery store chains have over food pricing laws
options.D: The total amount of food a farmer can produce in a single season

explanation: Purchasing power measures what an individual or family can actually afford to buy with available funds. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h6)

question: What body position should a patient be in during a nasogastric tube insertion?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: Flat supine position
options.C: High Fowler's position
options.D: Left lateral position

explanation: Sitting upright in high Fowler's position aligns the airway and esophagus properly, making safe tube passage much easier. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the best position for a patient who needs help with eating?

options.A: Flat on the back with neck extended
options.B: Semi-reclined at a 30-degree angle
options.C: Lying on the left side with knees bent
options.D: Sitting upright at a 90-degree angle

explanation: Correct! Sitting upright uses gravity to protect the airway and keeps food safely going down instead of into the lungs. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h4)

question: A patient with long-term diabetes complains of blurry vision and dark spots. Which eye problem should you suspect first?

options.A: Acute glaucoma
options.B: Retinal detachment
options.C: Nuclear cataracts
options.D: Diabetic retinopathy

explanation: Well done! Years of high blood sugar can damage the small blood vessels in the retina, making diabetic retinopathy a very common cause of vision changes. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T13#GNS324_U4_T13_h2)

question: Which parts of the body usually show signs of nutritional shortages first?

options.A: Deep dense bones like the femur
options.B: Hard cartilage located in the joints
options.C: Tissues with rapid cell turnover like skin and hair
options.D: Large skeletal muscles in the thighs

explanation: Cells that divide quickly need a constant supply of nutrients, so they show outward signs of shortage first. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T004#GNS227_U5_T004_h4)

question: What is a major operational challenge to routine immunization coverage in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of refrigeration units in primary clinics
options.B: Geographic barriers and hard-to-reach rural settlements
options.C: Too many trained nurses available for community outreach
options.D: A complete absence of infectious diseases in the country

explanation: Getting vaccines across rivers, bad roads, and remote terrain to reach every single child is one of our biggest field challenges. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h6)

question: A patient with kidney disease is given a standard dose of a drug that leaves the body through the kidneys. As a nurse, what is your best action?

options.A: Administer the medication twice as fast as doctor's orders
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink large amounts of grapefruit juice
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking all proteins in their daily diet
options.D: Monitor closely for signs of drug accumulation and toxicity

explanation: Great nursing care means anticipating problems! Since the kidneys are sluggish, the drug stays around longer, meaning we must watch the patient closely for accidental overdose signs. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h6)

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) in the hospital?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside nursing care with automated robots
options.B: To store a digital version of a patient's medical history and chart
options.C: To publish patient health data on public internet search engines
options.D: To track financial profits and billing for insurance companies

explanation: An EMR is simply the digital upgrade to old paper folders. It keeps all of a patient's history neatly in one place so your team can access it easily! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h1)

question: A patient on a harsh detox diet feels dizzy, weak, and has muscle cramps. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Sudden overproduction of essential vitamins in the liver
options.B: Rapid cleansing of toxins from the central nervous system
options.C: Electrolyte imbalances and severe caloric depletion
options.D: Increased metabolic efficiency burning excess fat stores

explanation: Starving the body of proper food and water messes up vital minerals (electrolytes) like sodium and potassium, causing weakness and cramps. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h4)

question: Why is the nurse often the first person to spot early signs of poor nutrition in a patient?

options.A: Nurses perform the initial admission assessments and spend the most direct time with patients
options.B: Nurses are legally responsible for preparing all hospital meal trays
options.C: Nurses hold advanced degrees in clinical biochemistry and food science
options.D: Nurses alone have the authority to prescribe therapeutic hospital diets

explanation: Spot on! Because you are right there at the bedside doing admissions and checking on patients constantly, you are in the best position to notice changes in their nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h1)

question: Which diagnostic imaging tool is most commonly used to identify structural brain abnormalities in a child with suspected cerebral palsy?

options.A: Abdominal ultrasound
options.B: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
options.D: Standard chest X-ray

explanation: An MRI provides detailed images of brain tissue, helping clinicians identify areas of past injury or malformation. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is a well-known risk factor for future violent behavior?

options.A: Consistently achieving a high level of formal education
options.B: Living in a household with little to no financial debt
options.C: Taking an active part in school or community sports
options.D: Experiencing abuse or trauma during childhood

explanation: Spot on! Early childhood trauma and seeing domestic abuse at home are strong warning signs for experiencing or committing violence later in life. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T14#GNS313_U3_T14_h3)

question: What does the term 'phenomenology' mean in psychiatric nursing?

options.A: The genetic mapping of hereditary psychiatric traits
options.B: The physical lab tests used to check blood chemistry
options.C: The subjective, lived experience of the patient's symptoms
options.D: The mathematical chance of making a full recovery

explanation: Phenomenology is all about stepping into the patient's shoes to understand what their illness actually feels like from their own unique point of view. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T1#GNS314_U1_T1_h4)

question: An unconscious accident victim is rushed in. What legal concept allows you to give emergency care without their verbal consent?

options.A: Expressed consent
options.B: Mandatory consent
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: Implied consent

explanation: You got it! When a patient can't speak and their life is in danger, the law assumes ('implies') they would want you to save their life. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of medication reconciliation in clinical practice?

options.A: To report pharmaceutical companies for high drug prices
options.B: To compare current medication orders against what the patient actually needs
options.C: To destroy expired medications found in the patient bedside locker
options.D: To calculate the total monthly cost of all prescribed drugs

explanation: Medication reconciliation is like a safety net! It helps catch missing medications that should be part of the patient's treatment plan. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T8#GNS215_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which set of vital signs shows that a patient's circulation is collapsing from an allergy?

options.A: Low heart rate and low blood pressure
options.B: High heart rate and low blood pressure
options.C: Low heart rate and high blood pressure
options.D: High heart rate and high blood pressure

explanation: As blood pressure drops, the heart beats much faster to try and make up for it and keep blood flowing. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is considered the most effective way to prevent the spread of infections?

options.A: Using private rooms
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns
options.D: Taking daily vitamins

explanation: Washing hands or using alcohol rubs removes transient microorganisms from the skin, stopping cross-contamination. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the main difference between primary and acquired immune deficiencies?

options.A: Primary deficiencies are always mild, while acquired deficiencies are fatal.
options.B: Primary deficiencies are present at birth, while acquired deficiencies develop later in life.
options.C: Acquired deficiencies can be cured with vitamins, but primary deficiencies cannot.
options.D: Primary deficiencies affect only red blood cells, while acquired deficiencies affect white cells.

explanation: Spot on! Primary immune conditions are inherited and present right from birth, whereas acquired ones happen due to outside factors later in life. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h1)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to tell normal sadness apart from clinical depression during an assessment?

options.A: To follow strict discharge rules set by the hospital administration
options.B: To prove to the family that the patient is faking their illness
options.C: To ensure the patient gets the right psychological or medical support
options.D: To avoid giving the patient any medications that lower blood pressure

explanation: It's normal to feel sad when facing a serious illness, but if it crosses into clinical depression, specialized counseling or treatment can truly help. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h5)

question: A nurse notices that the cleaning staff plugged an electric kettle into the same socket used for the vaccine refrigerator. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Leave both plugged in as long as the electricity is stable
options.B: Unplug the kettle and ensure the refrigerator has a dedicated socket
options.C: Move the kettle to another room only when patients are present
options.D: Switch off the refrigerator while the kettle is boiling water

explanation: Vaccine refrigerators must always have a dedicated power source to prevent accidental tripping or power overloads. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h3)

question: What is a frequent, painful problem caused by excessive pushing during bowel movements in pregnancy?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Placental abruption
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Hemorrhoids

explanation: You got it! Straining puts heavy pressure on the pelvic veins, which often leads to swollen, painful hemorrhoids (piles). [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h5)

question: Why is a speech therapist often called in to help patients with advanced neurodegenerative disorders?

options.A: To teach them foreign languages
options.B: To cure their underlying memory loss
options.C: To help manage swallowing and communication issues
options.D: To improve their walking balance and posture

explanation: Speech therapists do more than just speech—they train and protect the muscles used for swallowing, which stops dangerous choking and aspiration. Fantastic nursing awareness! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h6)

question: What does publishing nursing research primarily help the profession establish?

options.A: Total control over all medical school curricula
options.B: A unique and independent body of knowledge
options.C: The right to practice medicine without a license
options.D: Exemption from hospital ethical oversight boards

explanation: Spot on! Having our own distinct set of scientific knowledge is what truly makes nursing a respected, independent profession. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which tool is best for collecting a clean soil sample for microbial isolation?

options.A: A bare human hand pressed directly onto top dirt
options.B: An unsterilized wooden stick from the ground
options.C: A sterile trowel from a few centimeters below the surface
options.D: A household sponge soaked in soapy water

explanation: Well done! Digging slightly under the topsoil with a sterile tool helps you avoid dried-out dirt and outside germs. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h3)

question: What happens to the thymus gland as a person grows older?

options.A: It accumulates calcified deposits known as corpora arenacea
options.B: Its pinealocytes transform entirely into hormone-secreting neurons
options.C: It develops hollow colloid-filled follicles similar to the thyroid
options.D: It undergoes fatty involution and gradually shrinks in size

explanation: As we age, the active immune tissue in the thymus slowly gets replaced by fat cells—a natural process called involution. Nothing to worry about, it's just part of normal aging! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of 'task-shifting' in mental health care?

options.A: Moving patients from local clinics to foreign hospitals
options.B: Shifting all healthcare responsibilities away from nurses entirely
options.C: Training non-specialized health workers to deliver basic mental health interventions
options.D: Eliminating the need for any specialized psychiatric services

explanation: Spot on! Task-shifting helps bridge the gap by empowering everyday health workers and nurses to offer basic mental health care where specialists are few. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h7)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to study personality development?

options.A: It teaches the nurse how to permanently change a stubborn patient's basic character traits
options.B: It allows the nurse to legally diagnose psychiatric disorders without a doctor present
options.C: It helps the nurse look past challenging patient behaviors to build a better therapeutic relationship
options.D: It guarantees that patients will always follow medication schedules without asking questions

explanation: Understanding how personalities develop helps nurses see the root cause behind patient reactions, improving empathy and care. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is it important to encourage a labouring mum to empty her bladder regularly?

options.A: To speed up cervical dilation past 10 centimeters
options.B: To stop Braxton Hicks contractions from returning
options.C: To prevent the bladder from obstructing fetal descent
options.D: To collect urine for a daily routine glucose test

explanation: Brilliant! A full bladder gets in the way like a water balloon in the pelvis, which can slow down the baby's journey down the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h4)

question: Around which week of pregnancy do hCG levels usually hit their highest peak?

options.A: Around the tenth week
options.B: Right after delivery of the placenta
options.C: At the moment of fertilization
options.D: Just before active labor begins

explanation: That's right! hCG shoots up super fast in the early weeks and peaks right around week ten before starting to drop down. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T14#GNS121_U5_T14_h2)

question: In simple terms, what is osmosis?

options.A: The active pumping of mineral particles out of a cell using energy
options.B: The settling of heavy mineral solutes at the bottom of a container
options.C: The movement of blood cells through tiny capillary walls
options.D: The movement of water across a membrane toward higher solute concentration

explanation: Spot on! Water naturally moves toward areas with more solutes (like salt or sugar) to try and balance things out. Water always follows where the crowd is thickest! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T10#GNS121_U2_T10_h3)

question: How can a nurse best help a hospitalized older adult with severe arthritis eat on their own?

options.A: Insist that family members visit during every single mealtime
options.B: Feed the patient all meals to ensure they finish every single bite
options.C: Serve only pureed foods that require no physical chewing effort
options.D: Provide adaptive eating utensils like weighted handles or plate guards

explanation: Brilliant! Adaptive tools help work around stiff joints and tremors, letting patients keep their independence and dignity at mealtime. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T014#GNS227_U2_T014_h6)

question: What is one of the key roles of a nurse when acting as a facilitator in community mobilisation?

options.A: Writing laws that fine people who refuse to visit the clinic
options.B: Helping local committees run meetings and prioritize health problems
options.C: Taking over all financial accounts of the local government
options.D: Purchasing private cars for all members of the village council

explanation: As facilitators, nurses guide the process without dominating it, helping residents make their own decisions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which type of artificial fat, made by industrial processing, is best avoided entirely?

options.A: Monounsaturated fats
options.B: Naturally occurring saturated fats
options.C: Polyunsaturated fats
options.D: Trans fats

explanation: Trans fats are man-made to make processed foods last longer on shelves, but they are very hard on our hearts and best avoided. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h3)

question: What do we call the study of human tissues?

options.A: Cytology
options.B: Histology
options.C: Anatomy
options.D: Pathology

explanation: Histology is simply the study of tissues under the microscope. Think of it as zooming in to see how cells team up! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is nursing school unique compared to many other courses of study?

options.A: Clinical wards are always completely stress-free
options.B: Students must constantly jump between lectures and high-stakes hospital wards
options.C: All medical theory is learned strictly from storybooks
options.D: Nursing students never have to sit in a classroom

explanation: You have a big job! Nursing requires you to learn concepts in class and quickly turn around to apply them in real hospital settings where patients depend on you. [learn more](GST321_U8_T3#GST321_U8_T3_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of defibulation surgery in an FGM-affected woman?

options.A: To open fused scar tissue and restore normal drainage and function
options.B: To enhance the speed of weight loss
options.C: To permanently stop menstrual bleeding
options.D: To prevent future pelvic bone fractures

explanation: Spot on! Defibulation opens up the scar tissue seal to relieve urinary and menstrual blockages, preparing her safely for intercourse or childbirth. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the biggest advantage of using qualitative methods like focus group discussions?

options.A: They eliminate the need to ever write a formal report
options.B: They provide deeper insight into cultural beliefs and local attitudes
options.C: They require no active participation from community members
options.D: They give exact numerical percentages of disease outbreaks

explanation: Numbers are great, but talking to people helps you understand the "why" behind their health habits and cultural beliefs! [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is a dangerous method often seen in back-alley or clandestine terminations?

options.A: Receiving intravenous fluids at a primary health centre
options.B: Taking oral contraceptive pills prescribed by a pharmacist
options.C: Undergoing ultrasound scanning in a private clinic
options.D: Inserting sharp sticks or knitting needles into the uterus

explanation: Well done. Using crude objects like sticks is extremely dangerous and can easily cause severe bleeding and organ damage. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h2)

question: What is an essential nursing intervention during the postoperative recovery phase for a patient undergoing surgical repair of a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Applying dry heat packs directly to the perineal suture line
options.B: Encouraging heavy ambulation immediately after surgery
options.C: Maintaining continuous bladder drainage to keep the surgical site dry
options.D: Removing urinary catheters as soon as the patient wakes up

explanation: Keeping the bladder empty via a catheter prevents urine pressure from disrupting the delicate new suture line while it heals. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h6)

question: As you gently bend your patient's neck forward, they automatically bend their knees and hips. What sign is this?

options.A: Normal nuchal flexibility
options.B: A positive Brudzinski's sign
options.C: A negative Kernig's sign
options.D: Early signs of a stroke

explanation: That automatic knee-and-hip-bend when the neck goes forward is a classic positive Brudzinski's sign. It's a clear giveaway for irritated meninges! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T17#GNS222_U3_T17_h4)

question: How does breaking big, complicated tasks into tiny steps help a patient with a degenerative condition?

options.A: It speeds up the rate of cognitive processing in the brain
options.B: It ensures the patient never needs assistance from family members
options.C: It prevents feelings of overwhelming helplessness and promotes a sense of control
options.D: It cures the underlying muscle weakness completely

explanation: Mini-steps make daily activities feel doable rather than scary, helping patients hold onto their independence and confidence. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h4)

question: What makes the enteric nervous system so special compared to other parts of the peripheral nervous system?

question: Which type of estrogen is the strongest and most active during a woman's reproductive years?

options.B: Estradiol
options.C: Estrone
options.D: Eplerenone

explanation: Estradiol is the heavy hitter! It's produced in the highest amounts by the ovaries and drives most estrogen activity before menopause. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h2)

question: What do we mean by the "psychosocial impact" of an emergency?

options.A: The financial cost of rebuilding a damaged hospital
options.B: The physical injuries sustained during a natural disaster
options.C: How external events affect emotional and social well-being
options.D: Biological changes caused strictly by physical infection

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Psychosocial impact simply looks at how a crisis shakes a person's mental health, emotions, and relationships with others. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h1)

question: Which food nutrients are most important for keeping bones strong and posture upright?

options.A: Sodium and potassium
options.B: Vitamin C and iron
options.C: Protein and zinc
options.D: Calcium and vitamin D

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D are the ultimate dynamic duo for bone health! They build strong bones and help prevent weakness or spinal curving. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why might someone who eats enough food still experience cellular malnutrition?

options.A: They sleep fewer than eight hours every single night
options.B: They are consuming too much water with their meals
options.C: Their stomach physically shrinks from eating at irregular hours
options.D: Their body fails to properly process and utilise the ingested nutrients

explanation: Great thinking! Even with a full plate, cells starve if the body cannot properly break down, transport, or use those nutrients. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h1)

question: What is the biggest benefit of connecting a newly injured patient with a peer support group?

options.A: Speeding up bone healing through group social activities
options.B: Learning practical coping tips from others who share similar experiences
options.C: Replacing the need for professional medical nursing care entirely
options.D: Ensuring the patient never feels sad or angry about the injury

explanation: You nailed it! Peer mentors offer real-world advice and encouragement that textbooks just can't match. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T14#GNS225_U5_T14_h7)

question: Which type of precautions must you use for every single patient, no matter their diagnosis?

options.A: Standard Precautions
options.B: Airborne Precautions
options.C: Reverse Isolation
options.D: Contact Precautions

explanation: Spot on! Standard Precautions are our trusty baseline defense for every patient encounter because we never know an infection's status right away. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h2)

question: What happens to the mother's heart output right after the placenta is delivered?

options.A: It drops instantly to zero until diuresis begins
options.B: It experiences an initial rapid increase due to autotransfusion
options.C: It remains completely steady for exactly six weeks
options.D: It reverses direction and flows backward into the veins

explanation: You got it! Blood rushing back from the placenta temporarily boosts the heart's output right after delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: To isolate individuals with disabilities in specialized camps
options.B: To force families to relocate to urban rehabilitation centers
options.C: To make support services accessible at the grassroots level
options.D: To replace all tertiary hospitals with small village clinics

explanation: CBR brings care right to where people live, making sure help is close to home instead of locked away in distant city hospitals. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h4)

question: What feeding advice should a nurse give to a mother whose baby has acute diarrhea?

options.A: Stop all milk feeds for at least 48 hours to rest the gut
options.B: Withhold all food until the diarrhea stops completely
options.C: Replace breastmilk with plain water and sugar
options.D: Continue breastfeeding frequently throughout the illness

explanation: Never starve the gut! Breastfeeding gives the baby essential comfort, immune support, and nutrients to help them recover faster. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h7)

question: What usually happens if health spending has zero government regulation or control?

options.A: Equal distribution of doctors across all regions
options.B: Free medical supplies in every rural clinic
options.C: Automatic universal health coverage for all citizens
options.D: Inflated prices and unequal access to care

explanation: Without checks and balances, medical costs can skyrocket, making it impossible for everyday people to afford basic care. [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h1)
